x: On the same evening we were paid a very high compliment by Surrey A.C., who sent their strongest relay team (Griffiths, Higgins, Wigzell and Dacombe) to wrest from us the "Winstone" Trophy which we won last year at Hook.

Higgins, together with the Field Events Captain, have been the mainstay. We decided, in common with other clubs, to invite members of other clubs who would otherwise be short of competition, to assist us in carrying out our season's programme, and we have to thank A.
Higgins, another of our Juniors, did well to finish second.
Higgins also won three events by taking the weight, discus and javelin. The high jump brought out several new " Bels," some of whom we hope will turn out real good jumpers.
Higgins, has again shown excellent form and improvement on his last season's performances. His javelin efforts have shown most improvement.
100 yards (Juniors, not counting in match): 1 Garrett; 2 Macheli; 3 Higgins; 4 Driscoll; all of Belgrave.

Betterton found Higgins too good for him in the 440 Yards, but gave the winner a good race. Eric Bishop gained third place in the 880, and then in the 1 Mile we called upon Derrick Burfitt to assist us, and he simply walked away from his field, and Derrick certainly makes running look a very easy business.
Higgins, the Public Schools' quarter champion, beat Ted Read in the 220, and scored a double by also winning the 440, in which Jack Frost finished third.
McKenzie finished second in the 440 to Higgins in 51.9 secs. The 3 miles saw Len Herbert and Tommy Rowe out in front and after a good race Len triumphed in the good time of 14 min 39.8 secs.
Both the latter club and ourselves were poorly represented and as Herne Hill had Wilkinson and Higgins for the short sprints, they naturally scored major points in both these events.
Mackenzie, 110 ft. 7 ins.; 3rd, Higgins, 90 ft. 1 in. (Club record.) Shot Putt.—Pyramid Cup: 1st, Bergvalds, 35 ft. 7 ins.; 2nd, Melchoir, 34 ft. 4¾ ins.; 3rd, Higgins, 31 ft. 5½ ins.
Bill Sutton, Jock Mackenzie and Ans Bergvalds will be available for the Shot and Discus backed up by Doug. Childs, Terry Bateman, Len Higgins, Doug.
Ian Badiali won the 440 yds. in the good time of 51.5 secs., and Jack Brown was second to Terry Higgins in the 880 in 1 min. 57 secs., with Alan Bishop in third place
